```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B is a one-sided product. A single engineering team paying per seat counts as a paying customer, and Lody's $8–10/seat/month shows that price point already exists. A needs both sellers and active buyers, and its main fee is only paid when a deal closes. Brief A lists sales-cycle length as an open question, which makes a paid close within 90 days harder to reach.",
    "A's own evidence points against near-term revenue. A $750 Indie Hackers sponsorship produced 124 clicks and zero sales. The closest comparable, DealMyApp, reports healthy listings but weak buyer conversion. Three of five competitors charge 0% or near-0% commission, which removes price as a lever.",
    "B's demand quotes describe a concrete, recurring pain: agent work that teammates cannot see or steer. Several independent teams building the same feature set within months is cited as a sign of perceived demand, though that is still not evidence of paying demand.",
    "A carries more setup risk before revenue. It needs licensed third-party escrow, a state-by-state broker-licensing check, and handling of sensitive financial data, which the brief itself marks as unsourced. B's regulatory burden, a security and data-retention posture, mainly matters for enterprise pilots, and a first small-team customer may not require it.",
    "B has serious weaknesses of its own. Slack Code is free inside every Slack plan, which sets a $0 anchor. The six-week buildability claim and demand outside engineering are both [unsourced], so they count as missing. Even so, B's risks lower the size of the win, while A's risks block the first paid transaction."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's case for rests on the claim that a solo founder with AI agents can replicate Acquire.com's human 'acquisition expert' services (listing optimization, buyer vetting, deal coaching) at near-zero marginal cost. The cited source only describes what Acquire offers. Nothing shows agents can deliver those services or that this would solve buyer-side liquidity and trust. That gap matters because buyer liquidity and trust is the failure mode the brief itself documents.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both ideas face crowded markets with free or 0%-commission competitors, and neither brief offers direct evidence of anyone paying a new entrant. B wins mainly because its path to a first paid seat is structurally shorter than a two-sided marketplace's path to a first close, not because its demand evidence is strong. B's key feasibility claims are unsourced, and the free Slack Code anchor could erase willingness to pay."
}
```
